## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle interlinear-glossed exegesis of the dhāraṇīs in Amoghavajra's *Rénwáng jīng* recension (T246), giving phrase-by-phrase Sanskrit-Chinese semantic decoding in the *zhùyì* 注義 / *shì* 釋 format. Together with [KR6j0181](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0181) (T994 ritual manual) and [KR6j0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0184) (T995 abbreviated method), the text completes the Tang Esoteric ritual-exegetical apparatus around the *Rénwáng* corpus.

**Abstract**

The *shì* (exegesis) format mirrors Amoghavajra's *Uṣṇīṣa-vijaya zhùyì* T974D ([KR6j0155](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0155)) and his *Lǐqù shì* T1003 ([KR6j0193](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0193)) — providing phrase-level semantic-decoding of the dhāraṇīs to enable their integration with the *yoga-tantra* visualisation framework. The exegesis pairs each transliterated Sanskrit phrase with its Sino-Buddhist semantic equivalent and adds doctrinal-ritual context. This three-part structure (sūtra → ritual manual → exegesis) became the standard Amoghavajra Esoteric package, making the entire *Rénwáng* corpus exegetically tractable for the Tang and Heian-period Esoteric exegetical traditions. The principal Japanese exegete who built on Amoghavajra's *Rénwáng* commentary was Kūkai ([空海](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A9%BA%E6%B5%B7)) and his Shingon successors.
